generation.hypothesis: Liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu would selectively replace Ti/V-rich channels, creating a bonded, aligned RHEA–Cu composite with improved heat transport and He-blistering resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: The precursor would be an as-cast equiatomic WTaVTi single-BCC alloy containing about 71 vol.% W/Ta-rich dendrites and 29 vol.% connected Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.
generation.intervention: The vacuum-sealed precursor would be immersed in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h, using the Ti-rich regions as sacrificial pathways.
generation.conditions: Thermal conductivity would be evaluated from room temperature to about 800 °C and extrapolated above 1000 °C. Precursor dendrites would be screened with 25 keV He+ to approximately 8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2.
generation.structural_mediator: Dealloying should produce about 64 vol.% continuous BCC RHEA ligaments and 36 vol.% nearly pure FCC Cu channels, separated by an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer, with minor Ti-rich HCP precipitates.
generation.mechanism: Ti should mix with Cu and dissolve preferentially, while W, Ta, and V remain. Interfacial Ti extraction should trap immiscible W as a passivating, bonding layer. Aligned Cu channels should conduct heat, while reduced interfacial mismatch and increasing lattice transport should raise conductivity with temperature. Lattice complexity and strength should suppress He-defect migration, swelling, and cracking.
generation.predicted_outcome: Conductivity should increase from roughly 15–20 to about 75 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature, reach about 120 near 650 °C and 140 near 800 °C, surpassing W above about 650 °C. RHEA dendrites should show roughly 30% less blistering swelling than W and delayed blistering.
generation.baseline: Comparators would include untreated WTaVTi, pure W, pure Cu, conventional W–Cu, WTa, and WTaV.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis would apply to the segregated precursor and 1200 °C/96 h process. High-temperature W–Cu superiority would remain extrapolative, and irradiation claims would exclude neutron exposure, vacancy swelling, and direct composite irradiation.
generation.uncertainty: The dendrite irradiation response may not represent the finished interfaces and ligaments.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare treated and untreated specimens, verify architecture, then compare thermal transport and He+ response against the stated baselines.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis would be falsified if selective Cu replacement and the W-rich interlayer failed to form, or if conductivity did not substantially exceed untreated WTaVTi and surpass W near 650 °C, or if RHEA swelling and blister onset were not improved relative to W.

It correctly distinguishes direct composite thermal measurements from irradiation screening performed on precursor dendrites and appropriately limits claims concerning neutron damage, vacancy swelling, direct composite irradiation, and extrapolated high-temperature performance.
